Two more fixes to the socket, both found by the live run that `v0.4.0-preview.4` made possible. **90 of IBKR's 108 Trading endpoints, plus the socket**, as in `v0.4.0-preview.4`.

```sh
dotnet add package IbkrDotNet.Extensions.DependencyInjection --prerelease
```

## The socket is open before the session behind it is, and frames sent in the gap are discarded

`IbkrStreamingTransport` wrote solicited frames the moment the socket opened. A Client Portal Gateway completes the WebSocket upgrade locally — it logs `WebSocket handshake complete` — and only afterwards connects upstream, logging `connected to server`. Anything written in between is dropped without a reply ([#73](https://github.com/jerbersoft/ibkrdotnet/issues/73)).

So the first subscription on every connection, and every subscription a reconnect re-sent, could be lost outright. Nothing said so: the transport reported `Connected`, `SubscribeAsync` returned cleanly, `LastHeartbeatAt` advanced, and the subscription delivered nothing for the life of that connection. A reconnect walked into the same gap, which defeats the point of the transport holding subscriptions to replay.

An A/B against a paper gateway settles it. Same contract, same process, one difference: subscribing immediately gave **0 messages in 30 seconds**, with no `smd+…` anywhere in the gateway's log; the identical run delayed three seconds gave **4 frames and a full field set**. Downstream this had already been seen as `sor` and `str` never reaching the gateway across five sessions in a day, while the `uor` and `utr` unsubscribes at shutdown did.

The transport already recognised the confirmation and did nothing with it but log. It now opens a gate on the connection that every write waits on, so `ConnectAsync`, the connect inside `SubscribeAsync`, the reconnect path and the raw `SendAsync` are one rule in one place rather than three rules in three. `tic` is not exempt: it goes through the same send path, and a keep-alive for a session that does not exist keeps nothing alive.

The open itself waits too, so a gateway that never confirms fails once and loudly instead of leaving every later send to fail alone. The new `IbkrStreamingOptions.SessionConfirmationTimeout` bounds that wait at 10 seconds, the failure names it, and the socket is torn down rather than left behind.

Whether an OAuth socket confirms the same way is **not known** — the A/B above is gateway-only. Setting `SessionConfirmationTimeout` to `Duration.Zero` turns the wait off and restores the previous behaviour, so a caller who meets a socket that confirms differently is not waiting for a release.

This was unobservable before `v0.4.0-preview.4`: the confirmation arrives as a binary frame, and the transport discarded all of those.

## A `blt` bulletin carries `args` as an array

`StreamingBulletin.Args` was a single object, which is IBKR's published example. A live gateway sends an array, on all thirteen sessions it opened in a day, so a real bulletin failed to deserialize on the opening `[` ([#74](https://github.com/jerbersoft/ibkrdotnet/issues/74)).

This is the defect the previous release fixed for `ntf`, on the neighbouring topic, hidden the same way: the only fixture was IBKR's documented example, so the suite proved the shape IBKR publishes while nothing proved the shape IBKR sends. `Args` is now a list read so that the documented bare object still deserializes, as `StreamingNotification.Args` already was.

The capture shows two smaller disagreements, neither of them a failure. `id` is documented as a string and arrives as a number, which the library already read and a fixture now keeps read. And `exchanges` is sent, documented nowhere, and was null on every bulletin captured — so it stays unmodelled, with a remark saying it exists, rather than carrying a type nobody has evidence for.

The other unsolicited topics were checked against the same log and agree with their models: `ntf` was fixed last release, `act` and `sts` were already right. `sts` mattered most, because the transport reads it by hand and requires an object — had it been an array, `IsBrokerageSessionAuthenticated` would have stayed `null` forever with nothing to say why.

## What this breaks

`StreamingBulletin.Args` changes from `StreamingBulletinArgs?` to a list, so `bulletin.Args?.Message` becomes a loop or an index. That is the whole of the transcript's change besides the new option, and nothing else in the library read the type.

As with the `ntf` break last release, it is worth saying plainly: against a real gateway nobody can have been reading a `blt` message successfully, because every one of them arrived in the shape the old model rejected.

## Nothing else changed

571 tests, eight of them new. The scripted `WebSocket` now answers every connection with a binary session confirmation, because every real gateway does — which is what keeps the existing transport tests honest rather than merely green, and doubles as a standing guard on the binary-frame fix from last release.

Outside the packages, the live sweep gained a second market data check that asks which target IBKR restates for an exchange-qualified stream, since the wrong answer there is indistinguishable from no answer.

## Why this is still a prerelease

For the reason `v0.4.0-preview.1` gave — the public API is still settling — and because [#60](https://github.com/jerbersoft/ibkrdotnet/issues/60) is still open. Both fixes in this release come from driving the socket at a real gateway, and both were invisible to a suite that could only drive a fake. The sweep that would close #60, and the `.live.json` capture it tracks, are still to come.

## Publishing

Pushed by [Trusted Publishing](https://learn.microsoft.com/nuget/nuget-org/trusted-publishing) over OIDC, as the previous five versions were; both packages are also attached to this release.
